answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a fable as the anchor of the cost.
